what_happened: In job rxjg, the user corrected Athena's first reading of a retry request before work went on. The retry follows a verifier rejection of an earlier job on the landing-records change. The user gave three corrections. First, reconcile.rs also builds landing records through GitLandingRecords, so it must be updated for the content classification, and the 5 failing reconcile tests (cargo test -p athena-core reconcile::) must pass. Second, the owner-path fixture may use any directory name that has a nested .gitattributes holding '* athena-exclude' (owner-notes/ is fine). It must not use the word the boundary scan bans, and that part of the earlier criterion is dropped. Third, every caller of GitLandingRecords and pr_commits must be audited, including reconcile.rs and drain.rs. The event does not say what the first reading wrote. Judging by the corrections, it left out the reconcile.rs caller and the failing tests, and kept a fixture criterion tied to a specific directory name.
cause: The reading for a retry is built from the request text, and the previous verifier's findings are not carried into it as required items. Nothing in the reading stage enumerates all callers of a changed interface. So a second caller (reconcile.rs) and its failing tests went unnoticed until the user listed them. The reading stage also does not check its own criteria against the boundary-word rule. A fixture criterion that invited a banned word therefore stayed in until the user struck it. This is the same family of gaps as the earlier cases on this job family: follow-up readings take in only what the request says, not what the earlier stages decided or found.
prevention: For a request that follows a rejected or failed job, the reading stage should be given the prior verifier's findings and failed checks as structured input. The reading must then map each finding to a criterion, or say why it is dropped. For any change to a function or type, the reading stage should list every caller in the repo by search, and each caller should appear as a deliverable or an explicit exclusion. Fixture criteria should state the property needed (a nested .gitattributes with '* athena-exclude') rather than a directory name. A scan of the reading text against the boundary word list should run before the reading is accepted. A code check should refuse a retry reading that has no mapping for some verifier finding.
proposed_request: Retry the landing-records job that the verifier rejected. Make these three changes. (1) Update reconcile.rs, which also builds landing records through GitLandingRecords, for the content classification, so that the 5 currently failing reconcile tests pass (cargo test -p athena-core reconcile::). (2) The owner-path test fixture may use any directory name that has a nested .gitattributes holding '* athena-exclude'; owner-notes/ is fine. Do not use the word the boundary scan bans in any file, and drop the earlier criterion that named a specific directory. (3) Audit every caller of GitLandingRecords and pr_commits, including reconcile.rs and drain.rs, and make sure each one handles the content classification. Done when the full athena-core test suite, including the boundary scan and the budgets test, passes, and the changelog lists each caller that was changed.
